To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cellulase isozyme 9.5 increases during abscission, that the increase occurs before the decrease in cell wall integrity, and that cellulase is not present in the abscission zones prior to abscission.
The 9.5 cellulase isozyme is undetectable before the induction of absciession and is synthesized de novo.
cellulase activity in abscission zones is regulated by a complex mechanism involving the synthesis of new enzyme and a decrease in the level of the inhibitor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanism of abscission, the process by which the leaflet is separated from the rachis.
the study of the mechanisms of plant cell death and the regulation of programmed cell death (PCD) in plants.
the study of cell wall degradation in plant tissues and, more specifically, with the role of cellulase in the abscission process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzyme cellulase (EC3.2. 1.4) is involved in the abscission process of the primary bean leaf.
cellulase, as a group of enzymes, is involved in the hydrolysis of the abscising leaf.
the cellulase isozyme is not involved in wall hydrolysing during abscission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cellulases are synthesized de novo in abscission zone cells of bean, and that the 9-5 isozyme is the major form involved in wall hydrolysing activity.
cellulase activity increases prior to the loss of cell wall integrity in the abscission zones of bean leaves.

cellulase isozyme levels can be used as a marker of abscission and that the use of antibodies against specific forms of the enzyme is a useful tool in the study of cell wall metabolism.
